root_cause.text: In `drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_buffer.c`, `iris_create_internal_buffer()` added a newly allocated buffer to `buffers->list` before calling `dma_alloc_attrs()`, so a failed DMA allocation left a partially initialized buffer linked into the internal buffer list.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `list_add_tail(&buffer->list, &buffers->list);` to after the `dma_alloc_attrs()` success check and adds `kfree(buffer);` on failure, matching the CVE description that the old code returned `-ENOMEM` while leaving an invalid buffer in the list.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves `list_add_tail(&buffer->list, &buffers->list);` to after the `dma_alloc_attrs()` success check and adds `kfree(buffer);` on failure, matching the CVE description that the old code returned `-ENOMEM` while leaving an invalid buffer in the list.

intent_record.intent_summary: Delay list insertion until after successful DMA allocation and free the buffer on allocation failure to prevent invalid list entries and memory leaks.
intent_record.what: The call to add `buffer->list` to `buffers->list` was moved from before the DMA allocation to after a successful `dma_alloc_attrs()` call. In the failure path, a new `kfree(buffer);` was added inside the `if (!buffer->kvaddr)` block before returning `-ENOMEM`.
intent_record.how: Previously, a failed DMA allocation would leave a newly created buffer object linked into the list even though it had no backing memory, which could lead to later use of an invalid entry. With this change, the buffer is only published to the list after allocation succeeds, and allocation failure now frees the allocated `buffer` structure immediately to avoid leaking it.

grouping_result.intent: Delay list insertion until after successful DMA allocation and free the buffer on allocation failure to prevent invalid list entries and memory leaks.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the reported root cause by moving list insertion until after successful DMA allocation and handling allocation failure to avoid leaving a partially initialized buffer in the internal list.

candidates.rationale: This inserts the buffer into the internal list before DMA allocation succeeds. If dma_alloc_attrs() fails afterward, a partially initialized buffer remains linked, matching the root cause.
This is the allocation that can fail after the buffer has already been added to the list, leaving the invalid entry behind when the code returns -ENOMEM.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement adds the newly allocated buffer to the internal list before dma_alloc_attrs() succeeds, so if allocation fails the partially initialized buffer remains linked in the list.
This allocation can fail after the buffer has already been inserted into the list, leaving a broken internal buffer entry and triggering the vulnerability.
